text:
Tyson Foerster's slow start became a Philadelphia storyline this fall, and lately the headlines have flipped to him finding his game, with a three-point night in Ottawa. He has five goals and ten points in 25 games, and he skated on the top line with Christian Dvorak and Travis Konecny at practice this week.

The season line matches his chances. He has five goals on 5.7 expected, so nothing is running on luck in either direction, and his point rate (1.40 per 60) sits at the bottom of his talent range, which leaves room to climb. Philadelphia has scored 3.7 more goals than expected with him on. The five-on-five share is 45%, about a point better than without him. He's a physical winger (45 hits), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows he rarely carries the puck in (31% of his entries), so his line leans on dump-ins and the forecheck. Our range projects 30 to 49 points and 15 to 27 goals. Last season he played only 29 games.
